body.statement: For a finite family of SA-MPDAGs \(\mathfrak G=\{G_i\}\) and disjoint \(X,Y\), let \(A_i=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{G_i}(Y)\).  Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient criterion for simultaneous identification: each \(G_i\) has no proper semidirected path from \(X\) to \(Y\) beginning with an undirected edge, and for each pair \((G_i,G_j)\), either the relevant chain-component parent sets agree in both directions or the reweighted ancestral graphs \(\operatorname{RM}(G_i;X,Y)\) and \(\operatorname{RM}(G_j;X,Y)\) are Markov equivalent.

source.verbatim_statement: Given disjoint node subsets X and Y and a set of SA-MPDAGs G, let A_i=X intersect An_{G_i}(Y). If, for all G_i in G, there are no proper semi-directed paths from X to Y that start with an undirected edge, and for every pair G_i,G_j either the stated chain-component parent sets agree in both directions or RM(G_i;X,Y) and RM(G_j;X,Y) are Markov equivalent, then the causal effect of X on Y is simultaneously identifiable with the displayed identification formula.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published ICML 2025 author-repository PDF, Theorem 3.2, statement at page 3 and proof at page 7.
